title: soft panic suppressor and graceful queue drain hotpatch
author: Anika Patel
description: Motivation: A recent incident showed short-lived global spike events could trigger aggressive SLO circuit breakers and immediate tenant preemption, causing cascading request failures for a subset of customers. This PR introduces a 'soft panic suppressor' layer that transiently dampens aggressive SLO reconfiguration during burst windows and adds a coordinated graceful queue-drain path for nodes that are being reprovisioned or taken out of service. The approach aims to avoid unnecessary tenant quarantines while preserving long-term SLO enforcement. Changes: 1) New controller softpanic.Suppressor that tracks ephemeral surge tokens and applies a short holdoff window before escalating to tenant-level circuit trip. 2) Queue drain orchestrator that transitions in-flight request queues into a draining state and coordinates KV-cache flush with a fast-path fallback. 3) Load-shedding policy update: introduce a tiered preemption score that prefers best-effort queues during soft panic windows and defers hard tenant eviction for a configurable grace period. 4) Small API surface: a runtime flag (ENABLE_SOFT_PANIC) and two config knobs (panic_holdoff_ms, drain_soft_ttl_ms). 5) Unit + e2e tests and a runbook section for on-call. Rollout plan: feature-gate off by default for 24h canary in us-east-1 (10% traffic), monitor token-eviction and SLO error-rate, then rollout to remaining regions with a 2-hour ramp. Backport: critical hotfixs to release/2026-02 recommended. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked - [x] Tests (unit + e2e) - [x] Locally validated on canary cluster - [x] Runbook entries added - [x] Feature gate and config defaults set How to validate locally: run pkg/loadshedding/suppressor_test.sh and e2e/graceful_handoff_test.go. Related: ENG-4827 (stability incident follow-up).
